_comment: Machine-readable premium-apps capability overlay consumed by scripts/render_assets.py preflight step 23. Tier-A entries embed the capability list with a pinned 'verified_version'; Tier-B entries are detected at runtime via the installed app's default/authorize.conf because Splunk does not publish their capability reference.
_dedup_note: Splunk's own ES 8.4 capability page lists edit_notable_events, schedule_search, edit_managed_configurations, edit_lookups twice (once per feature); the entries below are de-duplicated.

SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite_v7._source_note: ES 7 has no standalone capability-reference page; the capability table lives in the 'Configure users and roles' topic of the 7.3 Installation manual.

splunk_app_soar._source_note: Previously pointed at the Splunkbase listing, which carries no capability information. The app's own 'Assign roles for Splunk App for SOAR' topic is the real reference, and it names only two app capabilities: splunk_app_soar_read and splunk_app_soar_write. There is no edit_phantom_* family and no splunk_app_soar_admin role; the two roles are the platform admin role and splunk_app_soar_dashboards. edit_soar_export belongs to the separate Splunk App for SOAR Export (Splunkbase 3411), which is a Tier-B entry, not to this app.
splunk_app_soar._admin_all_objects_note: Established by this sentence in the 'Roles for Splunk App for SOAR' table: the admin role 'includes the following capabilities: splunk_app_soar_read, splunk_app_soar_write, admin_all_objects, used to make modifications to Splunk App for SOAR.' The same topic's upgrade section reinforces that it is reachable on a non-admin role, instructing operators who cannot yet upgrade to 'remove any high-privilege capabilities that you added to the splunk_app_soar role, including the admin_all_objects capability.' Listed on this entry rather than inherited from the ES entry because the Splunk App for SOAR installs on a search head without ES.
splunk_app_soar._list_storage_passwords_verified_negativ: Verified negative. Neither the roles topic nor the upgrade guidance names list_storage_passwords for this app; admin_all_objects is the only platform capability it documents. Not added on plausibility.
splunk_app_soar._must_not_remove_note: splunk_app_soar_dashboards is the app's shipped least-privilege role, described as enabling 'a nonadministrative user to view Splunk App for SOAR dashboards.' Splunk does not publish that role's capability set, so splunk_app_soar_read is deliberately kept OUT of the disable list below: it is the read capability that role most plausibly depends on, and sweeping it could break dashboard viewing. Only the write capability and the platform capability are swept. Confirm the dashboards role against the installed authorize.conf before hardening, since the published topic does not enumerate it.

SA-ITOA._source_note: ITSI uses read_/write_/delete_/interact_with_ prefixes; there is no edit_itsi_* or configure_itsi_* family, and itoa_admin/neap_admin are roles, not capabilities.
SA-ITOA._platform_capability_note: ITSI 4.21 'Configure users and roles in ITSI' carries a section headed 'Splunk Admin capabilities and ITSI roles' whose opening sentence is: 'Some ITSI roles inherit capabilities that are typically only available to Splunk administration roles.' Its table grants six platform capabilities to non-admin ITSI roles: edit_token_http (all four roles), list_storage_passwords (itoa_analyst, itoa_team_admin), list_search_head_clustering and dispatch_rest_to_indexers (itoa_team_admin, itoa_admin), and list_settings and edit_monitor (itoa_team_admin). ITSI's own shipped [role_itoa_admin] stanza, quoted on the same page, confirms it under the comment 'Capabilities copied from Splunk admin role to enable write permissions', with list_storage_passwords = enabled. All six are listed below because ITSI can be installed without ES, in which case the ES entry never applies and they would go unswept. edit_monitor is the sharpest of them: it permits adding file monitor inputs, which turns into arbitrary local file read on a public-facing search head.
SA-ITOA._admin_all_objects_verified_negative: Verified negative. admin_all_objects appears in neither the 'Splunk Admin capabilities and ITSI roles' table nor the shipped [role_itoa_admin] stanza at 4.21, so it is deliberately NOT listed here. ITSI reaches stored credentials through list_storage_passwords instead. Do not add admin_all_objects to this entry without a documentation change.
SA-ITOA._must_not_remove_note: itoa_user, ITSI's own least-privilege default role, holds these read and interact capabilities plus a handful of writes that back drill-down and view state. write_itsi_deep_dive_context in particular is required the first time a reader drills into an auto-generated deep dive, so the write_itsi_* wildcard below must not be applied to them. Checked again when the six platform capabilities were added: of those, only edit_token_http is held by itoa_user, and ITSI grants it 'For event management' rather than for reading, so sweeping it from a purpose-built public reader breaks no read path. None of the six is matched by the write_itsi_* or delete_itsi_* wildcards, so no wildcard can reach them.

Splunk_TA_ueba._source_note: Previously pointed at Splunkbase app 4923, but this add-on is not distributed there: 'The Splunk Add-on for UBA is not available for download on Splunkbase. The add-on is installed by default with Splunk Enterprise Security (ES).' The capability name edit_uba_settings is correct and is confirmed twice, by 'Defines the edit_uba_settings capability which is added to the ess_admin role in Splunk ES and can be assigned' on this page and by the ES capability reference. Its default role is ess_admin, not admin.
Splunk_TA_ueba._platform_capability_verified_negative: Verified negative for both admin_all_objects and list_storage_passwords, and on a stronger basis than 'not documented'. The install-without-ES argument that justified adding admin_all_objects to the ARI and SOAR entries cannot apply here: Splunk_TA_ueba is not downloadable independently and ships only as part of the ES post-install configuration, so ES is present by construction and the ES entry, which already carries both platform capabilities, always applies. Adding either here would be pure duplication rather than gap coverage.
Splunk_TA_ueba._must_not_remove_note: No shipped least-privilege role of its own to protect. This add-on contributes a single capability to ES's ess_admin role rather than defining its own role hierarchy, so the least-privilege role that matters is ES's and is handled by the ES entries.

SplunkAssetRiskIntelligence._source_note: Every ARI capability carries the ari_ prefix; there is no edit_assets, edit_risk_*, edit_classifications, edit_exposure_analytics, manage_collections, configure_ari, view_ari_dashboards, or edit_ari_alerts capability, and ari_admin/ari_analyst are roles, not capabilities. ARI 1.0 also shipped ari_manage_posture_settings and named its least-privilege role 'user'; 1.1 renamed that role to ari_analyst and 1.2 no longer lists ari_manage_posture_settings, so do not carry it forward.
SplunkAssetRiskIntelligence._admin_all_objects_note: ARI documents admin_all_objects as a hard prerequisite for ari_manage_data_source_settings and ari_manage_metric_settings to function, and tells operators to satisfy it by assigning sc_admin or admin. An ARI deployment is therefore likely to have admin_all_objects granted somewhere reachable, so it is listed here rather than relied on from the ES entry: ARI can be installed without ES, in which case the ES entry never applies and the capability would go unswept.
SplunkAssetRiskIntelligence._must_not_remove_note: Deliberately empty, and verified rather than assumed. ari_analyst, ARI's own least-privilege default role, draws its read access from the ari_asset index, not from any capability, so no ARI capability is required for read-only investigation. All eight are writes: ari_edit_table_fields and ari_save_filters look reader-adjacent but only change which columns display and persist a filter, and both Discovery/Metrics/Investigation browsing works without them. This is the opposite of the ITSI case, where write_itsi_deep_dive_context genuinely backs a reader drill-down and must survive the write_itsi_* wildcard. Every name below is also listed literally, so no wildcard can over-match.
